title: Agent structures repeated, and in a harder setting
what: The agent-structure comparison (single plan, repeated planning up to three turns, planner plus challenger) had one run per structure and family on a five-drawing workspace. This record repeats it three times per case, and adds a harder setting: the six test families' thirty base drawings indexed together (a family of the same kind sits beside the asked one), twelve candidates returned instead of six, and a second query per family asking for the other material (AL6061). The expected verdict of every indexed drawing is computed from the gold facts (kind, value, material) and the free rules path reproduces all of them (integration test). Verdicts come from the deterministic verifier; the model chooses which lookups to make and when to stop. The OpenAI gpt-5-mini runs are from 2026-10-30; the Claude Haiku 4.5 runs, after the Anthropic balance was topped up, are from 2026-10-31 and sit beside them. Harness: src/fitwitness/evaluation/agent_trajectory.py (--repeats, --workspace, --materials, --top-k), manual workflow agent-trajectory.yml.
why_gpt_5_mini: the Anthropic account balance was empty on 2026-10-30, so the Claude repeat stopped after one repeat of two structures; the OpenAI adapter had never run this graph and needed a fix first (function calling for the plan schema, minimal reasoning for the reasoning model); Claude Haiku 4.5 was run on the same setting the next day (runs 41154974238 and 41155731372) and is recorded beside it, not in its place

runs.purpose: the original protocol repeated three times with Claude Haiku 4.5
runs.result: interrupted by an empty Anthropic balance (HTTP 400 'credit balance is too low'): repeat 0 of single plan finished 6/6 families with all 30 verdicts right, repeat 0 of repeated planning 6/6 with 30/30, repeat 0 of planner+challenger finished one family (5/5), then one call failed mid-run and the next run's first call was rejected, which stopped the batch; 39 runs were skipped. Model rows cost 0.07695 USD (the ledger counts 0.114548 because it keeps the reservation of the call cut off mid-flight). Too few runs to say anything about repeats.

one family: the first call of every structure was rejected by OpenAI (HTTP 400, invalid schema for response_format 'SearchPlan': additionalProperties must be false). The OpenAI adapter had never run the drawing graph. 0.0054 USD kept as a reservation.
one family after the adapter asked OpenAI for function calling: all three structures 5/5 ($0.0057). Not part of the numbers below.

runs.setting: easy: the family's five drawings indexed, six queries (one per test family, SUS304), 3 repeats per mode
runs.purpose: the original protocol repeated three times

runs.outcome: stopped by the ceiling, not by the work: with 0.862464 USD spent and a 0.04 USD per-run reservation the next run could pass 0.9, so 37 of the 108 planned model runs were not started: the whole third repeat (36) and the second repeat of planner plus challenger on FW-F029:AL6061. Repeats run: single plan 2, repeated planning 2, planner plus challenger 2 for eleven of the twelve cases and 1 for the twelfth.

findings: Easy setting, gpt-5-mini, three repeats: all 54 runs (18 per structure) finished with every verdict right and no invariant violation. All three structures are at the ceiling, so the setting cannot rank them. 4 plans needed one schema repair.

Hard setting: none of the three structures is near the ceiling. Runs with every verdict right: single plan 0 of 36, repeated planning 6 of 36, planner plus challenger 7 of 36. Verdict accuracy over all runs 54.8%, 64.1%, 61.6%; over the runs that finished 67.3%, 75.7%, 80.2%. The two readings order the multi-turn structures differently because the challenger runs also failed more often (9 of 36 against 6 and 7), so the data do not rank repeated planning against planner plus challenger.

Every wrong verdict is a drawing nobody looked up (not_inspected 112, 89, 64) or a run that ended before its verdicts (run_incomplete 78, 66, 98); inspected_wrong is 0 in all 108 runs. The model never misjudged a drawing it had inspected; it stopped before it had inspected them all (coverage before the first verdict 54%, 57%, 50%).

The single plan cannot cover twelve candidates by construction: a plan holds at most 8 operations, one lookup each, so it can inspect 8 of 12 (the nine tool calls are the search and eight lookups). Its 0 of 36 is the harness's shape, not a finding about the model; the two multi-turn structures have the turns to cover all twelve and still stopped early in most runs (stop reason plan_stop 24 and 17 times).
Runs ended in failure on a plan that did not fit the schema even after the one repair: 7, 6 and 9 of 36 (ValueError: model output failed schema validation). In the easy setting none failed.

The same case gave different verdicts across its three repeats in 5, 10 and 8 of 12 cases; no case was right in all three repeats under the single plan or repeated planning, and one under planner plus challenger (pass^3 0, 0, 0.083).
limitations: Two models in the repeated runs, each in its own runs: gpt-5-mini at minimal reasoning effort (2026-10-30) and Claude Haiku 4.5 without extended thinking (2026-10-31). The earlier partial Claude run (41030461645) was cut off by an empty balance after one repeat of two structures and is not used. Neither model's result says how a third model behaves, and earlier Claude single runs (agent-trajectory.json) are not comparable with these.

Twelve cases (six families x two materials) times three repeats: the repeats of a case are not independent, so counts of runs overstate how much was observed; 12 cases cannot rank two structures that differ by one or two cases.

The harder setting is hard by the harness's limits (at most 8 operations per plan, 16 tool calls, 4 model calls, 12 candidates), not by the drawings. The single plan's ceiling of 8 of 12 is one of them.

Retrieval is the same for every structure (drawing-number and BM25 channels, 12 candidates returned, all of the family's own drawings among them in every case); semantic and image channels are not part of this measurement.
Synthetic drawings. The verdicts are the deterministic verifier's; a failure here is a path failure, not a misjudgement.
Run costs are priced from third-party listings entered by hand; the OpenAI invoice is the truth.

The hard-setting Claude run has two repeats for the single plan and for repeated planning, and one or two for planner plus challenger, not the three planned: the 0.9 USD ceiling stopped it with 37 of 108 model runs not started. Compare shares, not run counts, between the two models' hard runs (108 against 71 runs).
findings_claude: Easy setting, Claude Haiku 4.5, three repeats: all 54 runs (18 per structure) finished with every verdict right, no invariant violation, no schema repair, no failed call. Same ceiling as gpt-5-mini: with either model the easy setting cannot rank the structures.

Hard setting, Claude: the single plan got 0 of 24 runs fully right (68.6% of verdicts) and the cause is the harness's shape: all 24 of its plans spent the 8 operations a plan can hold, so 4 of 12 candidates (2 of 10 in the two cases that retrieved ten) were never looked up; inspected_wrong is 0. Repeated planning got 22 of 24 runs fully right (99.3% of verdicts) and planner plus challenger 23 of 23 (100%): their later turns looked up the rest (coverage before the first verdict 69% and 67%; drawings never looked up at the end 0.08 and 0 per run).

Repeated planning's two misses are the same case in both repeats, FW-F029:SUS304: the run reached the 16-tool-call limit one lookup short and ended on budget_stop with one drawing unlooked (11 of 12 right). Planner plus challenger did that case right in both of its repeats. 23 of 23 against 22 of 24 is one case out of twelve and does not rank the two structures.

How the structures rank depends on the model. With gpt-5-mini at minimal effort repeated planning and planner plus challenger had every verdict right in 6 and 7 of 36 runs: it stopped early, and 6 to 9 of 36 runs failed schema validation. With Claude Haiku 4.5 they had every verdict right in 22 of 24 and 23 of 23 runs, with one schema repair in 71 runs. The two models are not like for like (a reasoning model at minimal effort against a model without extended thinking, different tool-call formats), so this says the structure comparison cannot be carried from one model to another, not which model is better.

Cost per model run: easy setting 0.0052 (single plan), 0.0051 (repeated planning), 0.0100 (planner plus challenger) USD, 0.366 USD for 54 runs; hard setting 0.0067, 0.0150, 0.0148 USD, 0.862 USD for 71 runs. The challenger's extra model call doubles the cost of a run in the easy setting; in the hard setting its cost matches repeated planning (0.0148 against 0.0150) and its result differs by one case.
